sections.value:
## A) Verdict

PASS for PR #246 at f3784caab656c1665c2daa469b283f60b2aa0065. No blocking correctness findings and no required code changes. Round 1 under C34; no further review round requested.

## B) Summary

Reviewed the frozen diff against main in the detached review worktree, the plan's four acceptance criteria, backpressure, tasks and live-proof record. The production change is confined to CLI receipt formatting and its API documentation. The recorded launch decision remains authoritative; no gate, daemon, store or wire behavior changes.

## C) Checks

- Spawn still applies the existing spawn_cli_response transformation, then passes its nested seat to the receipt helper. JSON serialization, raw refusal preservation and dispatched/bound/pid fields are unchanged.
- Revive emits through the same helper. Its existing cheap-compaction condition, compact message id and final compact result are preserved. No-wait spawn uses the same successful receipt path.
- emit_seat_receipt calls the original emitter first, preserves its exit status, and adds text only when !json && envelope.ok and the seat has a Copilot cache view. Setup errors return through their unchanged earlier paths. Refused spawn and revive therefore add no cache line; JSON adds none either.
- cache_proxy_view supplies both the recorded route and the established before-gate fallback, and returns None for other harnesses. Both reason and fix use the existing render::line, which handles line breaks, controls, frame markers and overlong text.

## D) Findings

None requiring changes. This is a correctness review with the requested launch-cost inspection, not a separate security-role verdict.

## E) Test quality and evidence limits

The new test has substantive expected-output assertions for proxied, plain with a fix, plain without a fix, before-gate fallback, non-Copilot omission and multiline reason/fix fencing. Omitting the rendered result or retaining multiline text contradicts those assertions. The pre-change source has no cache_route_line helper, so the new test cannot compile unchanged against it; that is not claimed as an executed behavioral RED result. No mutation run was performed.

The new unit test exercises the renderer, not its CLI wiring: removing a call to emit_seat_receipt would not fail that test. Existing shipped spawn/revive tests run the binary with --json and parse stdout; the author's committed proof additionally records a real human proxied spawn, a refused revive with no extra line, and a one-line JSON spawn receipt. I inspected that proof; I did not repeat live seat creation or exercise a real cheap revive. The shared helper and both guarded call sites were inspected directly.

## F) Acceptance and cost

- AC1: helper regression passed locally; spawn/revive wiring and fallback inspected; author live spawn receipt corroborates assembled output.
- AC2: success/JSON guards and unchanged earlier refusals inspected; existing exact-head CI integration suite passed; author refusal and JSON observations retained.
- AC3: multiline regression passed; reason and fix both reuse render::line.
- AC4: API prose matches the added line, optional fix, route-reading locations and the in-seat environment-check limitation.

Steady-state incremental cost is zero launches/second, with no poll interval or per-seat recurring work. There is no new loop, poll, timer, hook, sweep, request or process launch. Each successful human receipt performs an in-process route clone/string render and one additional stdout line. Neither a policy nor a brake: display only. No before/after fleet-rate measurement is claimed or needed for a change that adds no launch path.

## G) Validation

- just pr-freeze 246 --worktree: FINAL at the full head above; CLEAN, main base, latest checks passed, no migration changes.
- git diff --check origin/main...HEAD: passed.
- just shared-build --timeout 2 -- test --locked -p pij-cli --bin pij-rs a_copilot_receipt_line --then clippy --locked -p pij-cli --all-targets -- -D warnings: passed with the existing shared target selected through PIJ_SHARED_TARGET. The wrapper serialized the build, used nice 19 and capped jobs/test threads at four. One focused regression passed; macOS all-target clippy was clean.
- CI run 44425864565 at the reviewed head: all latest jobs passed. Rust test job 135230417759 reports 2,508 passed and six skipped; both JS checks and Rust lint also passed.
- harness checks --quick in the detached review worktree: exit 1, environment-limited. Seven sensors could not pass without local JS dependencies; lint resolved an incompatible ambient Biome. Pij-skill and native Copilot contracts passed; heavy Rust, route-inventory and smoke stages were skipped by --quick. Dependencies were neither installed nor borrowed. This is not a claim that the full local done gate passed.
- Initial canonical-checkout harness boot: passed readiness/typecheck/smoke; baseline orientation only, not exact-head PR proof.

## H) Handover and harness feedback

No correctness fix is owed before merge. Product sources remain unchanged by review. Use this verdict only for the full head above.

magicWand: extend the existing fake-daemon CLI tests with human stdout assertions for spawn/revive and unchanged JSON, so deleting either receipt call is caught without creating live seats. Captured as MW-001 in bucket pr246-review; optional follow-up, not a C34 gate.

difficulties: dependency-free review worktrees cannot run the JS-dependent local gate; exact-head CI is the available JS evidence. The shared-build lock correctly serialized the local Rust checks.
